title: Refactor sqlite db.py to a UserRepository class while keeping the existing API
description: Refactor the raw function-based database layer in python_sqlite_migration to a UserRepository class. Module-level functions (init_db, create_user, get_user, list_users) must remain as thin wrappers so existing tests continue to pass unchanged.

task_spec.prompt:
Refactor src/db.py to introduce a UserRepository class.

Requirements:
1. Create a UserRepository class with instance methods:
   - _conn(self) -> sqlite3.Connection  (reads module-level DB_PATH at call time)
   - init_db(self) -> None
   - create_user(self, name: str, email: str) -> dict
   - get_user(self, user_id: int) -> dict | None
   - list_users(self) -> list[dict]
2. Create a module-level _repo = UserRepository() instance.
3. Keep the existing module-level functions as one-line wrappers that delegate to _repo.
4. The monkeypatch pattern (monkeypatch.setattr(db_module, 'DB_PATH', ...)) must still work — _conn() must read DB_PATH from the module's global namespace at call time, not from __init__.

All 4 existing tests in tests/test_db.py must still pass.
Run: uv run pytest tests/ -v
required_artifacts: UserRepository class with _conn, init_db, create_user, get_user, list_users methods
_conn reads global DB_PATH at call time (not stored in __init__)
Module-level init_db, create_user, get_user, list_users delegate to _repo
success_criteria: uv run pytest tests/ -v passes (4 tests)
uv run python -c "from src.db import create_user" passes
followup_prompts: Run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `uv run pytest tests/ -v` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.

check_commands.build: uv run python -c "from src.db import create_user"
